heave.quantity: body (back) vertical displacement, peak-to-peak, fundamental only
heave.method: back-mounted 20 Hz accelerometer; least-squares fundamental + 2nd harmonic per 3-s flapping burst; displacement = a/(2 pi f)^2 (the 2nd harmonic adds only A2/(4 A1) = 6% in displacement, so the bob is close to sinusoidal)

heave.note: solo flight; pairs: -22.5% (-4.65 mm) at +18% frequency with unchanged dorsal acceleration p-p

heave.quantity: dorsal displacement amplitude (double-integrated dorsal acceleration; definition as the authors give it)
heave.note: consistent with taylor2019 if peak-to-peak: 20.7 mm x (5.48/7.05)^2 = 12.5 mm at the same acceleration
phase (0 = wingtip highest): shoulder highest at 0.53, lowest at 0.93 of the cycle
p-p of raw heave includes harmonics, so the implied displacement is an upper bound

rule_of_thumb: Body (back) heave peak-to-peak is about 2-3% of the wingspan in cruising flight: gull 39 mm / 1.34 m = 2.9%; pigeon 20.7 mm / 0.65 m = 3.2%; barnacle goose shoulder 15-31 mm / ~1.4 m = 1-2%. Displacement scales as acceleration / f^2: slower-beating big birds bob more in millimetres for the same g.

heave_phase.statement: Heave (dorsal) acceleration peaks in the middle of the downstroke (pigeon, accelerometer synchronised with 120 Hz video); a smaller peak at the start of the downstroke is sometimes visible (wing inertia).

Aerodynamic dorsal force is expected to peak mid-downstroke and the inertial (wing-acceleration) force at the start of the downstroke, so the dorsal-acceleration maximum falls between the start and middle of the kinematic downstroke and the minimum between the start and middle of the upstroke.

Body displacement is the double integral of that acceleration: with a near-sinusoidal signal the body is LOWEST where the acceleration is highest (early-to-mid downstroke) and HIGHEST early-to-mid upstroke. Barnacle goose shoulder (wind tunnel, 16 m/s): highest at 0.53 and lowest at 0.93 of the cycle (0 = wingtip at the top). Combined: the body moves opposite to the wings with a lag - it is lowest from late upstroke to mid-downstroke and highest from the end of the downstroke to mid-upstroke.
heave_phase.source: dimitriadis2015, krishnan2022, taylor2019 (inference stated as such)

heave_phase.statement: Lesser black-backed gull heave acceleration falls from its maximum to its minimum in 0.405 of the cycle (IQR 0.387-0.423; 60 461 cycles) and recovers in 0.595: the acceleration waveform is skewed (2nd harmonic 23% of the fundamental at +0.29 cycle). Taylor et al. 2019 take max->min dorsal acceleration as the downstroke phase; it lags the kinematic stroke by under a quarter cycle, so this is a proxy, not the kinematic downstroke share.
heave_phase.where: this task, work/lbbg/stats.json heave_maxmin_share (estimator gives 0.50 on pure sinusoids)

surge.phase: surge acceleration maximum precedes the heave acceleration maximum by 0.18 cycle (resultant length 0.90): the body traces a tilted ellipse in the vertical plane, near quadrature
surge.note: surge axis also picks up g x sin(pitch) from any body pitch oscillation; treat as an upper bound on the true fore-aft motion

pitch.quantity: within-wingbeat body pitch and roll oscillation during slow (3.3 m/s) 90-degree turns
pitch.note: slow manoeuvring flight, an upper bound; no measurement of body pitch oscillation in cruising large birds was found

body_angle_mean.quantity: body angle to horizontal, mean per speed

body_angle_mean.values: 5-21 deg, falling with speed; ~40% drop from 4 to 6 m/s; 5-8 deg above 11-12 m/s

body_path_template.species: Larus fuscus (lesser black-backed gull), wild, 7316 flapping bursts
body_path_template.phase_zero: maximum of the FUNDAMENTAL of the heave (dorsal) acceleration; the raw acceleration maximum lies between the start and the middle of the kinematic downstroke (taylor2019), at mid-downstroke in a video-synchronised pigeon (krishnan2022)
body_path_template.reading: body lowest at phase 0, forward-most at ~0.32, highest at 0.5, rear-most at ~0.82: a near-vertical ellipse, the body surging forward as it rises
body_path_template.columns: phase (cycles), heave acceleration (fundamental = 1), heave displacement (peak-to-peak = 1), surge displacement (same scale as heave displacement)
body_path_template.scale: heave displacement peak-to-peak = 39.2 mm (median) = 2.9% of span; surge displacement peak-to-peak = 12.0 mm (upper bound)
body_path_template.note: built from the median fundamental and 2nd-harmonic amplitudes and phases; individual bursts vary (see variation.json)
